## Exchange before a single-block stage (`MeshBlock.forward`) {#sec-ch01-block-forward}

### Summary

A driver that steps one block calls `MeshBlock::forward` once per stage. That call does two things in a fixed
order: it first refreshes the ghost cells from the neighbours, then advances the stage. The order matters
for a caller that edits the interior between two calls, because the edit reaches the ghosts before the next
reconstruction reads them.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** N/A, a code map: exchange the conserved ghosts, then run `advance_local`.

**Data.** In: `hydro_u` and `scalar_s` with stale ghosts. Out: the same tensors advanced by one stage.

**Placement.** Once per stage, from the single-block driver.

**Activation.** Always exchanges first; no ordering switch.

**Guarantee / limits.** Changes data freshness, not the stencil order; the mesh driver orders it differently.

**Evidence.** No dedicated test (missing evidence); the ownership rule is tested in @sec-ch11-timing.
:::

### Derivation

No separate derivation: this section describes an interface or control-flow path, and the operators are derived
in their owning chapters.

### Numerical method

`MeshBlockImpl::forward` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::forward >}}) calls `exchange_ghost_zones` and
then `advance_local`. `MeshBlockImpl::exchange_ghost_zones`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange_ghost_zones >}}) exchanges the conserved hydro state and the
scalar densities with interpolation on. It then re-applies the non-outflow $x_1$ boundary functions on the tangential
ghost slabs the exchange owns (the `refresh` closure; @sec-ch11-timing), and recomputes the scalar ratios. A reflecting
wall whose tangential faces are all exchange-owned is re-applied in one call over the full extent; it writes the same
slab values and rewrites the other rows with the values they hold. The mesh
driver `MeshImpl::forward` ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::forward >}}) advances first and exchanges afterwards
(@sec-ch01-mesh). The wrapper changes when the ghosts are fresh, not the stencil order; physical boundary conditions
and cubed-sphere interpolation keep their own errors.

@fig-ch01-block-forward-flow shows the call sequence.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch01-block-forward-flow
#| fig-cap: "Exchange before a single-block stage. Labelled green boxes name operations or owners; black arrows show the reading sequence, not a timing measurement."
#| fig-alt: "Sequence: caller modifies interior; conserved exchange; advance_local; physical boundary fill."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch01.figures.fig_block_forward_flow import make_fig
make_fig()
```

**Why exchange first.** Two facts of the code decide the order.

1. The reconstruction of a stage reads ghost cells (@sec-ch04), so the ghosts must hold the neighbours' current values
   when the stage starts. The exchange at the top of `forward` guarantees that for a single block
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::forward >}}).
2. A driver may change the interior between two calls (the kinetics step of @sec-ch01-driver does). With the exchange
   first, that change reaches the ghosts before the next reconstruction; with the mesh order it reaches them only
   after the next stage.

: Implementation anchors for the block-level forward. {#tbl-ch01-block-forward-code}

1. Exchange, then advance: `forward` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::forward >}}).
2. Fill the layout ghosts, refresh the $x_1$ wall corners, recompute the scalar ratios:
   `exchange_ghost_zones` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange_ghost_zones >}}).
3. Compare with the mesh order, advance then exchange: `MeshImpl::forward`
   ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::forward >}}).

**How to use it.** There is nothing to configure. The whole method is two calls
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::forward >}}):

```cpp
void MeshBlockImpl::forward(Variables &vars, double dt, int stage) {
  exchange_ghost_zones(vars);
  advance_local(vars, dt, stage);
}
```

A driver that edits `hydro_u` between calls must edit the interior only; ghost edits are overwritten by the
exchange on the next call.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The source comment on `forward` attributes a removed cubed-sphere seam bias to this placement; the chapter
does not promote that comment to measured evidence. A regression that isolates driver-split sources between
consecutive calls is missing.
:::
